source: https://www.shelaghlewins.com/tablet_weaving/patterns_past.php — 'Narrow Oseberg Band' (instruction sheet: https://www.shelaghlewins.com/tablet_weaving/Oseberg_narrow/Oseberg_narrow.pdf). Threaded-in / warp-twined band from the Oseberg ship burial, Vestfold, Norway, c. 834 AD; 10 tablets, all turned forward together every pick (not double-face, not brocade, not twill). Card colours and S/Z threading transcribed pixel-by-pixel from the PDF's Figure 6 threading chart (a vector diagram, not a photo), which independently agrees with the PDF's prose description ('Tablets 1-3 and 9-10: four yellow'; 'Tablets 4, 8: four blue'; 'Tablets 5, 7: one blue, three yellow'; 'Tablet 6: alternating blue and yellow') and with the explicit setup instructions ('turn tablet 5 so the blue thread is in position A', 'tablet 6 ... positions B and D', 'tablet 7 ... position C'). The 8-pick colour sequence below was derived from the document's own rotation diagrams (Figure 3: position labelling; Figure 4: which physical hole moves to which position on a forward turn) plus the explicit instruction order 'turn ... and pass the weft' (turn happens before the weft that becomes a pick, i.e. pick 1 is read after the first turn) — not by running this library's code. It was then cross-checked qualitatively against the woven-band photograph (Figure 1): the photo shows a period-4 zigzag running mid-tablet, outer-tablet, mid-tablet, opposite-outer-tablet, matching the derived sequence's column-6/7/6/5 oscillation, with a measured pixel period of ~59px for 4 picks, consistent with the plateau widths seen at the start of the photographed run. Confidence: high for the card setup (an unambiguous vector chart, triple-confirmed against prose and instructions); high-but-not-absolute for the pick-to-rotation phase alignment, which rests on the document's diagrams and wording rather than the photo (a mirrored photo would look identical either way, so the photo confirms shape/period, not absolute phase).
